Subject: Initial cluster constraints and questions for Redwood private deployment

Hi Connor —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We are starting to sketch the on‑prem footprint for phase 1 of the private deployment. A few constraints from our side:

- 3 racks in our primary datacenter (zone-a, zone-b, zone-c)
- GPU hosts will be limited to a single rack initially (due to cooling); most inference will run on mixed CPU/GPU pools
- We need PII logs to never leave our VPC and prefer nodeLocal or hostPath caching where possible

Questions:
1) How tight should we make node pool sizing for the Redis/KV cache pods vs. the inference workers?
2) Recommendations for PVC/io class mapping for models with heavy KV cache churn
3) Any opinion on using local NVMe for prefix cache + replicated NFS for model artifacts?

Attaching a short worksheet of our rack counts and expected qps.

Appreciate any high‑level guidance — we can set a working session if helpful.

—Alex
Alex Garcia

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the worksheet. Quick answers up front, then I suggest a 45‑minute architecture review where we walk the numbers.

- Node pool sizing: keep inference workers and KV/cache in separate pools. Start with a 70/30 split (worker/cache) by CPU for mixed pools, but pin GPU hosts only to worker pools. That gives predictable CPU headroom for model orchestration when GPUs are busy.

- PVC mapping: prefer local NVMe for ephemeral prefix/KV caches (fast, low latency). Use a ReadWriteMany or NFS mount for large model artifacts if you need shared access across replicas. If you can tolerate model copies, copy artifacts to local disks on deploy and serve locally for fastest inference.

- Local NVMe + replicated NFS: that pattern works — NVMe for hot KV/cache, replicated NFS or object store for cold models and artifact distribution. Ensure the deployment has an automated sync/validate job to keep local copies consistent.

I'll attach our on‑prem checklist and a sample node profile matrix. Hannah and Marissa — please add anything I missed.

Next steps: suggest Tue 8 May 10:30 ET for a walkthrough?

Thanks,
Connor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial cluster constraints and questions for Redwood private deployment

Connor / Alex —

A couple of practical rules we've used on similar installs:

- Failure domains: treat each rack as a failure domain and spread the worker replicas across racks. Put the cache replicas on at least two racks to tolerate a single rack failure.
- Node classes: create node pools with labels: node.k8s.redwood/role=worker, node.k8s.redwood/role=cache, node.k8s.redwood/role=infra (for monitoring, ingress, control-plane aware pods).
- Taints/tolerations: add a NoSchedule taint on GPU-only nodes and use tolerations only for inference pods that need GPUs. Avoid scheduling control-plane pods to GPU nodes.
- Storage performance: we recommend two storage classes: fast-ssd-local (local NVMe, block) and shared-nfs (replicated, tunable r/w). Set reclaimPolicy=Delete for cache PVs and Retain for model artifact PVs.

Also: run a small PV IO soak test (fio) with the model cache pattern — I can share the script.

—Hannah
Director, Platform Solutions

Subject: Re: Initial cluster constraints and questions for Redwood private deployment

Alex —

A few pragmatic config snippets to consider (high level):

- Storage classes:
  * fast-ssd-local: provisioner: local-volume, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, reclaimPolicy: Delete, mountOptions: ["noatime"]
  * shared-nfs: provisioner: nfs-client-provisioner, reclaimPolicy: Retain

- PVC sizing: cache PVs: start with 200GB per cache replica for medium models (scale after soak). Artifact PVs: 2–4TB per node if you want to keep local model copies for 20–30 models.

- KV cache eviction: aim for a cache hit rate >= 85%. If you can't reach that, increase cache size rather than adding pods; the cache is more efficient than pulling extra worker pods.

- Network: prefer nodeLocal DNS + kube-proxy in IPVS mode; colocate monitoring agents on infra nodes to reduce noise on worker pools.

I can paste an example StorageClass YAML in the call.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer

Quick, pragmatic checklist before the call:

1) Confirm kernel and iommu settings on NVMe hosts (list files: /etc/modprobe.d/ and sysctl entries)
2) Provision an operator that will seed models to local disks (we use an init job that verifies checksums)
3) Add a kubelet config with reserved cpu/memory for system daemons (10% of CPU or min 2 cores)
4) Test egress rules to ensure telemetry endpoints for Redwood console are reachable from control plane subnets (or configure STUB collector if you require no outbound).

I'll prepare a small runbook of commands and an example DaemonSet for the seeder.

—Dev
Platform Engineer
